subject: Biotechnology
title: Organic vs Biotech Farming
description: Learn Organic vs Biotech Farming in one minute.

hook.text: Organic bans GMOs — biotech embraces them. Are these two farming philosophies enemies or potential allies?

buildup.text: Organic farming relies on natural inputs and crop rotation — lower yields per hectare but less chemical pollution.

discovery.text: Gene editing could create crops with traits organic farmers want — disease resistance without foreign genes or chemical sprays.

twist.text: Organic certification excludes all genetic engineering by definition — even gene edits indistinguishable from natural mutations.

climax.text: Some scientists advocate a middle path — combining agroecology with precision genetic tools for sustainable intensification.

punchline.text: Nature or technology? The answer may be both — sustainable farming needs every tool.

quiz.question: Why might gene editing appeal to organic farming goals despite being excluded from organic certification?
options: Gene editing is cheaper than organic certification
Gene editing can create disease-resistant crops without foreign genes or chemical sprays, aligning with organic principles
Gene editing makes crops grow faster than organic methods
